origin.description: Produces a Digamma generalized linear model family object. The Digamma distribution is the distribution of the unit deviance for a gamma response.

arguments.name: theta
arguments.text: Numeric vector of values of the canonical variable, equal to -1/phi where phi is the dispersion parameter of the gamma distribution.

origin.details: Suppose that y follows a gamma distribution with mean mu and dispersion parameter phi. Write d(y,mu) for the gamma distribution unit deviance. Then meanval.digamma(-1/phi) gives the mean of d(y,mu) and 2*d2cumulant.digamma(-1/phi) gives the variance. cumulant.digamma is the cumulant function; meanval.digamma gives the first derivative and d2cumulant.digamma gives the second derivative, which is the variance.

translation.description: Second derivative of the Digamma-family cumulant K(theta); the variance at canonical parameter theta.

arguments.name: theta
arguments.text: NumPy array of canonical parameters, equal to -1/phi where phi is the gamma dispersion parameter.

translation.details: Evaluates 2*(1/theta + trigamma(-theta)), with the same large-|theta| asymptotic patch as R when theta < -1e3. Trigamma uses recurrence plus the package logmdigamma port for digamma.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from statmod.d2cumulant_digamma import d2cumulant_digamma

theta = np.array([-1, -0.5, -0.1])
print(d2cumulant_digamma(theta))
